data.gender_notes: Raffaele is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew name 'Rapha', meaning 'heal' or 'God heals'. In Christianity, Raffaele is the Italian version of the name Raphael, referring to the archangel known for his healing powers. The name Raffaele carries the meaning “God heals” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Raffaele usually hope their child will grow to embody god heals and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of healing, compassion, and divine intervention.
data.etymology: Raffaele belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God heals.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Raffaele total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: רפאל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: רפאל הוא שם שמשמעותו 'אלוקים רפא' או 'רפואה של אלוקים', ומקורו בשורש העברי 'רפא' שפירושו 'לרפא' או 'להבריא'. השם רפאל מופיע בספרות היהודית והנוצרית כאחד, ומשויך למלאך הרפואה והמרפא.

in_greek.name: Ραφαήλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ραφαήλ είναι το ελληνικό ισοδύναμο του εβραϊκού ονόματος רפאל (Rafae'l), που σημαίνει 'Θεός ιαμάται' (Θεός θεραπεύει) ή 'ιαματικός του Θεού'. Το όνομα Ραφαήλ απαντάται στην Καινή Διαθήκη και στη μεταγενέστερη εκκλησιαστική παράδοση.

in_latin.name: Raphael
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Raphael derivatur ex hebraeo רפאל (Rafae'l), quod significat 'Deus sanat' vel 'Deus est sanitas'. In traditione christiana, Raphael est unus de septem archangelis, minister sanitatis et medicinae.

in_english.name: Raffaele
in_english.long_meaning: The name Raffaele originates from the Hebrew name רפאל (Rafae'l), which means 'God heals' or 'God is health'. This name is associated with Raphael, one of the seven archangels in Christian tradition, known for his role in healing and medicine. The name Raffaele has been used across various cultures and is a popular choice for boys in many Christian communities.

data.cultural_impact: Raffaele is a popular name in Italian culture and is often used to honor the Catholic saint, St. Raphael, who is the patron saint of travelers. In Italy, it is common for parents to give their children names with religious or historical significance, making Raffaele a name deeply rooted in Italian heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Raffaele holds deep spiritual significance as it is derived from the name Raphael, which means 'God heals'. This name is a reminder of the healing powers of God and the love and care He shows towards His children. Raffaele can serve as an inspiration to seek God's healing power in times of need and to trust in His love and mercy. Additionally, the name Raphael also represents the archangel Raphael, who, in the Book of Tobit, traveled with and healed Tobit and Sarah, demonstrating the power and compassion of God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Raffaele, meaning "God healed" in Italian, symbolizes the healing power of God in our lives and the hope for divine intervention during times of illness or hardship. It is a reminder of God's compassion and love, and the belief that He can restore health and wholeness in those who seek His mercy.

historical_references.reference: Raffaele Sanzio was an Italian painter and architect of the High Renaissance period. He was born on April 6, 1483, in Urbino, Italy, and died on July 6, 1520, in Rome, Italy. He is best known for his paintings, which include the figures and vivid colors.

Raffaele Calcagnini, also known as Raphael Borghini, was an Italian art historian and biographer. He was born around 1483 in Borgo San Lorenzo, Italy, and died around 1557. He is best known for his biography of Raffaele Sanzio, which was published in 1550.
